summary: South Carolina's AG has opposed federal preemption of state AI law and co-led the 44-AG child-safety letter; chatbot bills (S. 1037 / H. 5476) never left committee in 2026. Nothing specific to frontier or catastrophic risk.

items.title: S. 1037 — Protecting Children from Chatbots Act
items.text: Referred to Senate Labor, Commerce and Industry and did not advance before the 2025-26 session ended; House companion H. 5476 also stayed in committee.

items.title: AG letter opposing the federal 10-year state AI moratorium
items.text: Wilson and a bipartisan AG coalition urged Congress to drop the moratorium on state AI laws.

profile.headline: South Carolina is landing billions in Google data centers while at least 13 of its counties have paused new ones, and the governor has declined to call for a statewide pause.

sections.text: South Carolina has no governor's executive order on AI; the Department of Administration published a state AI Strategy in March 2024 and runs an AI Center of Excellence for agencies. In September 2026 Gov. Henry McMaster said he would not call for a statewide data-center moratorium. No moratorium bill passed in 2026, but the budget requires large data centers to report water use. State-owned utility Santee Cooper charges higher rates to users needing 50 MW or more.

Google announced on October 13, 2025 a $9 billion investment through 2027 to expand its Berkeley County campus and build two campuses in Dorchester County, on top of $3.3 billion announced in September 2024.

At least 13 counties, including Colleton, Spartanburg and York, had passed data-center moratoriums by late September 2026. Colleton adopted a six-month pause on July 7, 2026 after about 500 people protested a proposed project; Spartanburg froze new applications in June 2026. Lexington, Kershaw and McCormick counties were considering pauses. Bills in 2026 proposed a statewide moratorium (S. 5526) and an end to incentives (H. 4583).
South Carolina State University, an HBCU, announced a collaboration with NVIDIA in June 2026 on AI education and workforce development.

In July 2026 Sen. Tim Scott, chair of the Senate Banking Committee, asked Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh to address data centers and AI at a coming hearing, raising their water and electricity use amid rising utility costs and resistance in South Carolina.
